evals.prompt: We're a 4-person team of React/TypeScript web developers. We need an iOS and Android app for our field-service product: technicians work in basements with no signal, take photos, fill forms, and sync later. Some customers want a home-screen widget later. Which stack and how should we structure it?
evals.expected_output: Recommends React Native + Expo given the team, with native navigation primitives, and flags widgets as native-module work (expo-widgets or native targets). Designs offline-first: local SQLite as source of truth, write-local-then-sync with an outbox and idempotency keys, background sync with exponential backoff, explicit conflict policy, photo uploads via background transfer, and offline UX (pending badges, last synced). Includes an ADR-style rationale with rejected alternatives.
expectations: Recommends React Native with Expo (or clearly justifies another choice) based on team skills
Makes the local database the source of truth that the UI reads from
Specifies queued/lazy writes with idempotency keys for offline form submissions
Names an explicit conflict resolution policy
Mentions background sync with exponential backoff
Notes that widgets need native code or a native-module package

evals.prompt: Our Android app takes 3.5 seconds to show the first screen on a mid-range phone and scrolling the feed stutters. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: Measures first with release builds on a mid-tier device (Macrobenchmark, TTID/TTFD, JankStats/Perfetto), then applies top fixes: Baseline/Startup Profiles, deferring SDK init, no main-thread I/O, render cached content first, SplashScreen API; for scrolling: stable keys and contentType, immutable models, deferred state reads, sized/cached images. States budgets (under 1 s target start, 16.7/8.3 ms frames, frozen frames > 700 ms).
expectations: Recommends measuring on a release build and a physical mid-tier device before changing code
Recommends deferring or lazily initializing SDKs and removing main-thread I/O
Mentions stable keys for lazy list items
States a frame-time budget (16.7 ms at 60 Hz or 8.3 ms at 120 Hz)

evals.prompt: We use Expo. Can we push a new checkout feature to users with EAS Update tonight instead of waiting for App Store review?
evals.expected_output: Explains that OTA updates are for fixes and small changes within reviewed functionality; adding a new feature that changes the app's reviewed functionality violates Apple's rules (DPLA 3.3.1(B), App Review 2.5.2), and native code changes can't ship OTA. Recommends shipping through review behind a feature flag, using OTA only for fixes, runtime-version binding, and gradual rollout with rollback.
expectations: Does not recommend shipping a substantially new feature via OTA to bypass review
Cites Apple's rules on downloaded or interpreted code (DPLA 3.3.1(B) or App Review 2.5.2)
Mentions that native code changes require a store build
Recommends a feature flag and/or staged rollout for the new feature

evals.prompt: What corner radius should our Android bottom sheet use?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: a visual Material question for android-design, not an architecture question. Answers briefly (extraLarge, 28 dp top corners) or defers to android-design without producing a stack decision or layer diagram.
expectations: Does not produce a stack recommendation, architecture layers, or sync design
Answers with the Material shape token (extraLarge / 28 dp) or refers to android-design
